headline: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5, nearly matching Fable 5 for half the price
summary: Anthropic's new Claude Opus 5 model offers capabilities close to its top-performing Fable 5 model, but at half the price. It also features enhanced cybersecurity safeguards.
details: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 5, a new AI model designed for complex coding, knowledge work, and enterprise workflows. The company states Opus 5 comes close to the capabilities of its top-performing Claude Fable 5 model, but is available at half the price.

Opus 5 also boasts stronger cybersecurity safeguards compared to its predecessor, Opus 4.8. This comes after government concerns regarding the previous Fable 5 model, which led to weeks of negotiations and new AI regulation discussions.

Pricing for Opus 5 is set at $5 input and $25 output per million tokens, making it more cost-effective than Fable 5 and slightly cheaper than OpenAI's GPT-5.6. This release subtly addresses recent controversies over alleged hidden usage caps and the AI money squeeze.

Customers can also opt for a "Fast mode" in research preview, offering higher speeds at double the standard price. An automatic fallback option to a lower-tier model is available when safeguards mandate declining a user request.

headline: Sam Altman's World raises $52.5M in crypto sale with 12-month investor lockup
summary: The biometric verification startup, co-founded by OpenAI's Sam Altman, secured funds through a WLD token sale, demonstrating long-term investor commitment with a one-year lockup.
details: Sam Altman's biometric verification startup, World, has successfully raised $52.5 million through a crypto token sale to strategic investors. These investors participated in a 12-month lockup sale of World's WLD token, signaling a strong long-term commitment to the project's growth. The funds will be directed to the World Foundation, based in the Cayman Islands, to support the expansion of World's network.

World's core mission is to provide "proof of human" tools for online verification, addressing the increasing challenge of distinguishing human users from bots and AI agents. It aims to popularize its World ID, an anonymous digital marker that confirms a human is behind an account. This system is designed to combat the proliferation of AI-generated content and bot activity online.

To obtain a verified World ID, users must undergo an iris scan by an "Orb," a metallic device that converts their unique iris pattern into a cryptographic identifier. These Orbs are deployed at World's offices and partner locations globally. This biometric verification method is central to ensuring the integrity of the World ID system.

Operated by Tools for Humanity, World began as "Worldcoin" and rebranded amidst broader crypto industry backlash. Despite launching a new app version in April and securing partnerships with companies like Tinder, Zoom, and Docusign, the project has faced challenges in scaling its business and gaining widespread consumer adoption. The company also conducted layoffs in June.

Pantera Capital led the sale, a venture capital firm specializing in digital assets. Other notable participants included Eightco Holdings, Bain Capital Crypto, Susquehanna Crypto, and Selini Capital. This diverse investor group underscores the strategic interest in World's unique approach to digital identity.
